hero.headline: The Scrum Credential
hero.subtext: Backed by the Institute of Scrum, our endorsed credentials set a higher standard — recognizing professionals who deliver results in the real world and stand apart through demonstrated skill, judgment, and impact.
hero.source: Endorsed certifications require 20+ hours of structured learning and a rigorous 45-question examination — because your credential should prove what you can do.

trustedBy.title: CERTIFIED SCRUM — POWERING THE WORLD'S BEST TEAMS

roleSpecialized.title: Role-Specialized Depth
roleSpecialized.description: Dedicated tracks for Scrum Master, Product Owner, and Scrum Facilitator. Each certification addresses the specific competencies, challenges, and career outcomes of your chosen role — not a one-size-fits-all overview.

masteryPath.title: Three-Level Mastery Path
masteryPath.description: Progress from Foundation through Practitioner to Authority as your experience grows. Each level builds on the last, creating a clear career trajectory that employers recognize and reward.

practicalFocus.title: Practical Application Focus
practicalFocus.description: Every certification requires 20+ hours of structured self-paced learning and a rigorous 45-question examination. You earn your Endorsed credential by demonstrating what you know and can apply.

foundation.title: Foundation Level
foundation.description: Perfect for those new to Scrum or transitioning into Agile roles. Validates your understanding of core Scrum principles, roles, events, and artifacts.
foundation.audienceDesc: Ideal for professionals entering Agile environments who want to build a solid Scrum foundation with a recognized, role-specific credential.

practitioner.title: Practitioner Level
practitioner.description: For experienced professionals who facilitate Scrum events and coach teams. Demonstrates ability to apply Scrum in complex, real-world environments.
practitioner.audienceDesc: Designed for experienced Scrum practitioners who actively facilitate events, coach teams, and apply the framework in complex real-world environments.

authority.title: Authority Level
authority.description: The highest tier — for senior practitioners shaping Agile strategy at the organizational level. Validates deep expertise and thought leadership.
authority.audienceDesc: For senior Agile leaders shaping organizational strategy, mentoring Scrum teams, and driving enterprise-level transformation.

earn.title: Earn Your Credential
earn.description: Successfully pass the exam and receive your digital Scrum certification.

whyChooseUs.description: A credential from Institute of Scrum is a validation that you have proven practical, role-specific mastery through rigorous assessment. When employers see this designation, they know the holder has earned standards that go far beyond attendance and memorization.

sections.rolePlayHighlight: Built for the Role You Actually Play
sections.rolePlaySubtitle: Most Scrum certifications treat every role the same. Institute of Scrum takes a fundamentally different approach. Our certification system provides dedicated learning tracks for each Scrum role, with three progressive levels that mirror how professionals actually develop expertise. Whether you facilitate sprints, own the product vision, or design collaborative workshops, your certification should reflect the depth of what you do.
sections.threeLevelsSubtitle: Three distinct professional tracks. Three levels of mastery. One rigorous standard of excellence.

allCertsAtGlance.description: Your next career milestone starts here. Choose your role, select your level, and begin earning the Endorsed credential that proves what you can actually do. With 20+ hours of structured self-paced learning, no prerequisites, and a rigorous examination, you are investing in a credential built for the long term.

ctaBanner.headline: Ready to Validate Your Scrum Expertise?
ctaBanner.description: Join thousands of professionals who've advanced their careers with Institute of Scrum certifications.

Each cell displays the full certification name and links directly to its dedicated detail page, giving visitors a clear path to explore every credential available across our learning framework.

foundation.name: FOUNDATION
foundation.desc: The Foundation level establishes essential Scrum knowledge and core principles for those entering the field. Candidates demonstrate understanding of foundational frameworks, terminology, and practices required to participate effectively in agile teams and begin their professional journey.

practitioner.name: PRACTITIONER
practitioner.desc: The Practitioner level validates the ability to facilitate Scrum events, coach teams, and apply the framework in complex environments. Candidates demonstrate active mastery through scenario-based assessment grounded in real-world practice.

authority.name: AUTHORITY
authority.desc: The Authority level confirms senior-level expertise and thought leadership in Scrum. Candidates demonstrate the capacity to shape Agile strategy at an organizational level, mentor practitioners, and drive sustainable transformation across enterprise contexts.

benefits.confidence: Builds confidence before the final test

howItWorks.description: Our mock exams are designed to reflect the actual certification test. Each test follows the same structure, timing, and level of difficulty to ensure a realistic experience.

01.title: Start the mock exam
01.body: Select your certification and launch the timed practice test — structured exactly like the real thing.

02.title: Answer questions within the time limit
02.body: Work through scenario-based questions under real test conditions, managing the countdown timer.

03.title: Review each question carefully
03.body: Flag questions you're unsure about and revisit them before submitting — just like the real test.

04.title: Submit the test
04.body: When you're ready, submit your responses and receive your score instantly.

05.title: Review your results and performance
05.body: Get a full breakdown by topic area — identify where you excelled and where to focus your study.

intro.description: Project management is the practice of planning, organizing, and guiding work from start to finish — ensuring the right things get done, on time, and within budget. In a world where businesses juggle competing priorities at every turn, it has become one of the most essential disciplines driving efficiency, innovation, and results across every industry.
intro.badgesAlt: ESM, ESM-P, and ESM-A certification badges

whyMatters.title: Why Scrum Master Matters
whyMatters.point1: Organizations lose an average of 11.4% of their investment due to poor project management — Scrum Masters directly reduce that risk.
whyMatters.point2: Scrum Masters act as a shield for their teams, enabling developers to focus on delivering value without distraction.
whyMatters.point3: They foster a culture of transparency, inspection, and adaptation — the core pillars that make Agile transformation sustainable.
whyMatters.point4: Certified Scrum Masters are consistently linked to faster delivery cycles, higher team morale, and measurable productivity gains.

whoShouldLearn.title: Who Should Learn
whoShouldLearn.point1: You don't need a specific degree — anyone with a passion for collaboration and continuous improvement can become a Scrum Master.
whoShouldLearn.point2: Team leads and project managers looking to transition from command-and-control to servant leadership.
whoShouldLearn.point3: Developers or QA engineers who want to expand their impact beyond technical tasks.
whoShouldLearn.point4: Business analysts and product stakeholders who want to better understand and support Agile delivery.
whoShouldLearn.point5: HR professionals and organizational coaches driving culture and change management programs.
whoShouldLearn.point6: Recent graduates and career changers seeking an in-demand, globally recognized Agile credential.

careerOpportunities.title: Career Opportunities
careerOpportunities.point1: Demand for skilled project managers and Scrum Masters is growing across all industries — tech, healthcare, finance, and beyond.
careerOpportunities.point2: Certified Scrum Masters command a significant salary premium compared to non-certified practitioners.
careerOpportunities.point3: The role opens pathways to Agile Coach, Release Train Engineer, and Head of Delivery positions.
careerOpportunities.point4: Global organizations actively recruit ESM holders to lead digital transformation and hybrid Agile programmes.
careerOpportunities.point5: With ESM, ESM-P, and ESM-A you build a structured career path with a recognized credential at every stage.

intro.description: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the Scrum team’s work. They define product backlog priorities and align stakeholder expectations with business goals and the actual development roadmap.
intro.badgesAlt: EPO, EPO-P, and EPO-A certification badges

whyMatters.title: Why Product Owner Matters
whyMatters.point1: Organizations waste millions due to misaligned product priorities — a skilled Product Owner prevents this directly.
whyMatters.point2: The PO acts as the bridge between business strategy and delivery teams, ensuring every sprint generates real value.
whyMatters.point3: They maintain a clear, ordered Product Backlog that keeps teams focused on the highest-impact work.
whyMatters.point4: Certified Product Owners consistently link business objectives to development outcomes, accelerating product–market fit.

whoShouldLearn.title: Who Should Learn
whoShouldLearn.point1: Anyone with a passion for product strategy and delivering customer value can become a Product Owner.
whoShouldLearn.point2: Business analysts and requirements managers looking to take ownership of product direction.
whoShouldLearn.point3: Project managers transitioning to product-centric, outcome-driven ways of working.
whoShouldLearn.point4: Entrepreneurs and startup founders who want to structure their product development with Agile discipline.
whoShouldLearn.point5: Marketing and UX professionals who want a formal role in shaping what gets built and why.
whoShouldLearn.point6: Recent graduates and career changers seeking a high-demand, globally recognized product leadership credential.

careerOpportunities.title: Career Opportunities
careerOpportunities.point1: Product Owner roles are among the fastest-growing positions in tech, finance, and digital transformation initiatives.
careerOpportunities.point2: Certified POs command premium salaries and are often fast-tracked to Senior PO or Head of Product positions.
careerOpportunities.point3: The role opens pathways to Product Manager, Chief Product Officer, and Agile Portfolio Manager.
careerOpportunities.point4: Global organizations actively seek EPO holders to align product roadmaps with business strategy.
careerOpportunities.point5: With EPO, EPO-P, and EPO-A you build a complete, internationally recognized product leadership career.

faq.description: Everything you need to know about the Product Owner role, the certification journey, and what to expect once you’re certified — answered in plain language.

certPath.whoShouldPursueDesc: Define product vision, manage the backlog, and maximize value delivery with stakeholder alignment and business acumen.

intro.description: The Scrum Facilitator is the expert in designing and running effective Scrum events. They create psychologically safe environments that foster collaboration, collective decision-making, and continuous improvement across Agile teams.

whyMatters.title: Why Scrum Facilitator Matters
whyMatters.point1: Poor facilitation leads to unproductive meetings and disconnected teams — Scrum Facilitators transform sessions into aligned, outcome-driven conversations.
whyMatters.point2: Scrum Facilitators create the conditions for high-performing teams by ensuring every voice is heard and every decision is informed.
whyMatters.point3: They apply proven facilitation techniques to sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives that drive real, measurable improvement.
whyMatters.point4: Organizations with skilled Scrum Facilitators report higher team engagement, faster decision-making, and reduced conflict.

whoShouldLearn.title: Who Should Learn
whoShouldLearn.point1: Anyone who regularly leads or attends Scrum events and wants to make them more effective.
whoShouldLearn.point2: Scrum Masters looking to deepen their facilitation toolkit beyond framework basics.
whoShouldLearn.point3: Agile coaches and organizational change managers seeking structured facilitation credentials.
whoShouldLearn.point4: Team leads and managers who run workshops, retrospectives, or cross-functional alignment sessions.
whoShouldLearn.point5: HR professionals and training specialists who design collaborative learning experiences.
whoShouldLearn.point6: Consultants and coaches who want a recognized credential in professional facilitation.

careerOpportunities.title: Career Opportunities
careerOpportunities.point1: Skilled facilitators are in high demand across Agile, organizational development, and change management disciplines.
careerOpportunities.point2: The ESF credential distinguishes practitioners who can run effective events from those who simply attend them.
careerOpportunities.point3: Certified Scrum Facilitators progress to Senior Agile Coach, Organizational Change Lead, and Workshop Design roles.
careerOpportunities.point4: Global enterprises invest in facilitation capability as a strategic lever for digital transformation and culture change.
careerOpportunities.point5: The ESF certification is your entry point to a recognized facilitation career path within the Institute of Scrum ecosystem.

faq.description: Everything you need to know about the Scrum Facilitator role, the certification journey, and what to expect once you’re certified — answered in plain language.
